title: Grateful Dead Live at Cumberland County Civic Center on 1982-09-17

ai_review.summary: A solid recording (minor cut at the end) captures a high‑energy show highlighted by an explosive post‑drums sequence despite mid‑set lulls and intermittent Lesh drop‑outs.
ai_review.review: The performance is buoyed by standout moments like Candyman, Althea, High Time, the Space > Spanish Jam > Other One suite, Morning Dew and a ripping Sugar Magnolia. While the new material (West L.A., Throwing Stones, Touch of Grey) and occasional bass disappearances create some mid‑show drag, the overall energy is high and the post‑drums jams are electrifying. The recording is generally clear but loses the final minutes of the drums segment.

ai_rating.rationale: The review praises many high‑energy sections and a decent sound, offset by noted mid‑set lull and a missing drum ending; overall rating lands solidly at four stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear overall capture described as 'fantastic', but the last few minutes of the drums track are cut, indicating a minor technical flaw.

standout_songs: Space > Spanish Jam > The Other One
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is engaging but hampered by new, undercooked material; the second set builds momentum with strong jams, though Lesh's intermittent drop‑outs interrupt flow until he returns for powerful bursts. The post‑drums sequence provides the show's climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia 'noodles nicely' and drives the jam with strong, inspirational playing throughout, especially in Morning Dew and Sugar Magnolia.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh delivers spectacular bursts ('Lesh‑Bomb') that elevate the music, but his bass drops out several times—possibly due to equipment issues—causing brief momentum loss.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir adds intensity by joining Garcia in the jam and pushing the envelope during the post‑drums sections.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum track is solid ('Drums is drums') but the recording cuts off the final minutes of the set.
